chunks: If the servant confesses against himself to theft, his hand is not cut off; but if two witnesses testify against him, it is cut off.
And what he narrated does not contradict these reports:
Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb, from al-Faḍl, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: the servant; here, the accused person
key_terms.شَاهِدَانِ: two witnesses whose testimony establishes the claim
key_terms.قُطِعَ: the hand was cut off as the legal hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: Does a thief’s own confession establish the hadd punishment in Shia fiqh, or is witness testimony required?
ai.summary: This passage concerns a legal ruling on theft and distinguishes between confession and testimony in establishing the hadd punishment. It also introduces a transmitted report through a sanad from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام in the context of reconciling narrations on the issue.
